To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the service industry has a shortage in the talent pool of workers with the skills, competencies, and characteristics that it requires.
the Malaysian service industry has a shortage of employees who possess competencies that are critical to service delivery and that are in high demand by employers.
Malaysian human resources managers perceive a gap between the competencies they seek and the skills and characteristics that are available in the talent pool.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the skills and talents that service industry employers seek, and the ease of recruiting individuals with such skills and talents.
the identification of the most important skills and attributes for the services workforce and the extent to which the talent pool in the Malaysian service industry can meet those needs.
understanding the nature of the gap between industry needs for skills and competencies, and the availability of such skills within the talent pool.

there is a gap in the availability of the talent pool in the Malaysian service industry.
there are gaps between the needs and availability of skills and talent among service industry workers, and these gaps can be attributed to a variety of factors.
there exists a gap between industry requirements and the availability of talent pool in the service industry.

Malaysian service industry employers are concerned about the availability of workers with certain skills and characteristics.

the service industry in Malaysia is facing a serious talent shortage.
